corrections: Article limitation on the retrobulbar spot sign reworded: abstract 75% vs results 78% (7/9) kept as an unreconciled conflict; the Figure 1 caption shows six patients without claiming they are all patients with the sign.

Article limitation on CRAO diagnosis extended: abstract 88% diagnosed vs 38% ophthalmology-confirmed, plus the methods describing all included patients as having a CRAO diagnosis and the results reusing 88% for embolic risk factors.

Article limitation on treatment extended to name the second single-patient mention (vision improved from light/colour to hand motion) alongside the teenager given intra-arterial TPA; both kept aggregate.
Added a limitation on percentages that do not resolve to whole patients of nine (38%, 88%, 40% of the HBOT group).
Added a limitation that Video S1 frames carry burned-in screen text (site/system header and a partly masked fragment in the date position); categories only.
unresolved: Disposition aggregate_only: the source reports nine patients only as a series (percentages and means); no patient has individual identity evidence, so no individual patient records are created and series statements are not copied to placeholder patients.
reported_individual_count is 9 (literal) and roster_complete is false because none of the nine stated individuals can be enumerated.

Source conflict on the proportion with a retrobulbar spot sign: the abstract states 75% while the results state 78% (7/9). The Figure 1 caption shows the sign in six distinct patients without saying that these are all patients with the sign. These are not reconciled.

The abstract states that 88% of patients were diagnosed with CRAO while the results and discussion state that 38% had an ophthalmology-confirmed diagnosis by fundoscopic examination; the denominators and the relation between these figures are not stated. The methods describe all included patients as having a diagnosis of CRAO, and the results give the same 88% for patients with risk factors for embolic occlusive disease; the abstract's 88% is not reconciled with either.

The results give 67% undergoing hyperbaric oxygen therapy and 40% of those with subjective improvement, one patient whose vision improved from recognising light and colour to recognising hand motion, and one teenager receiving intra-arterial TPA who did not recover vision, without saying which patients; these two single-patient mentions have no case narrative or link to Figure 1 or Video S1, so no individual record is created and none of this is assigned to individuals.
Figure 1 shows six unidentified series members; ownership is unresolved and it is not EHR-includable. Supplement Video S1 is a single ocular ultrasound clip whose patient is not identified.

Several series percentages do not resolve to whole patients of nine (38% and 88% of nine, and 40% of the 67% undergoing hyperbaric oxygen therapy); denominators are not stated, so these are arithmetic ambiguities, not values assigned to anyone.

Video S1 frames carry burned-in screen text, including a site/system header and a partly masked fragment beside the on-screen clock in the date position; categories only are recorded in the supplement manifest.

key_findings: Aggregate-only disposition is correct: nine patients are reported only as series means and percentages; the teenager given intra-arterial TPA and the patient improving to hand motion are isolated one-sentence mentions with no case narrative, no link to Figure 1 or Video S1, so no individual record is created.
Roster: reported_individual_count 9 from the literal Results sentence; roster_complete false.

Video S1: six sampled frames viewed; on-screen site/system header, R EYE label, probe/preset text, clock and a masked header region with a fragment in the date position.
residual_risks: Two single-patient sentences could be argued to individuate patients; kept aggregate because neither has identity evidence beyond one descriptor plus one treatment/outcome.
Series percentages are internally inconsistent with nine patients; recorded as limitations only.
